claims.hypothesis: Is the steep central dust temperature rise caused by AGN-heated dust?

claims.result: Central T = 57.1 K before subtraction; profile flat afterwards
claims.finding: The temperature gradient is due to an unresolved warm dust component associated with the AGN

evidence.quote: The unresolved warm dust component also explains the steep temperature gradient, as the temperature profile derived after the point source subtraction is flat.

claims.hypothesis: Does a two-component dust model including AGN-heated warm dust describe the global SED better, and how does it change the SFR?
claims.experiment: Two-greybody fits (thin and with free tau) and STARDUST fits constrained by decomposed point source fluxes
claims.finding: Previous SFR (5040 Msun/yr) overestimated by about a factor of three

evidence.quote: a factor of three smaller than previous estimates due to a large AGN contribution

referee_caveats_inferred: Fiducial beta fixed from the global SED (with the 160 um point excluded) for all pixels, so spatial beta gradients are not constrained
AGN warm component temperature is poorly constrained (87 +34/-18 K) and rests on only two point-source fluxes plus the integrated SED
Decomposition assumes [C II] morphology equals cold dust morphology, even though a central [CII]/FIR deficit is admitted
Dust-based gas surface density assumes a constant gas-to-dust ratio from a single global CO(2-1) based estimate with alpha_CO = 0.8
Inconsistent redshift values printed (4.4704 vs 4.4074) and 57.1 vs 57.7 K central temperature between text and conclusions
